construct.diagnosis_or_process: Hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria due to SLC34A3 dysfunction
construct.mechanism: SLC34A3 encodes the proximal-tubule sodium-phosphate cotransporter NaPi-IIc. Loss of function causes renal phosphate wasting and hypophosphatemia. The low phosphate appropriately stimulates 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, increasing intestinal calcium absorption and producing hypercalciuria—a key discriminator from FGF23-mediated hypophosphatemic disorders.

second_answer_attack.resolution: Both cause renal phosphate wasting, but FGF23 excess suppresses or inappropriately normalizes calcitriol and typically does not cause the marked hypercalciuria of HHRH. High calcitriol plus hypercalciuria and SLC34A3 point to NaPi-IIc loss.
